clue.text: Firm heavy blows — they're responsible for the strain

definitions.note: plural kitchen tools through which liquids are poured off; the noun 'strain' is the act of straining

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm
landers is slang for heavy punches that land on target

explanation.surface: A company boss's heavy-handed tactics are blamed for the stress on the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' suggests stress or tension, but it is the kitchen sense: draining vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is the perforated bowl used to drain food, so such bowls do the straining.

clue.text: Striking approach brings pay-off!

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
to approach is to come near

explanation.surface: A forceful negotiating stance gets a payout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like 'impressive' but means on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A pay-off in the sense of a final result or consequence is what an outcome is.

clue.text: Leaning on a nag — it's to be broken

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart and reassembled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone propped against an old horse that is to be broken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be broken' rearranges A NAG IT'S. 'Broken' suggests breaking in a horse, which suits the nag.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resting against a wall is leaning on it: a prepositional synonym.

clue.text: Woman medico getting sick in America

parts.note: a medico is a doctor, abbreviated DR

indicators.note: in says one word is placed inside another

parts.note: USA, the United States of America
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A female doctor falls ill while in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is only a link; 'Woman' as a bare definition stands for any female first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Drusilla is a female first name, so the bare word 'Woman' stands for it as an example.

clue.text: Holy men are not commonly seen on board

indicators.note: being on board a vessel puts a thing within the two letters of the ship

parts.note: on board means aboard ship, and SS is the abbreviation for steamship
ain't is the colloquial form of are not

explanation.surface: Religious men are rarely found aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention: the piece goes inside SS (steamship), so AINT sits between the two S's. 'Commonly' marks dialect, not frequency.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints are people of exceptional holiness, so holy men is a plural description of them.

clue.text: Like money, there for using — hang staying in the black!

indicators.note: one word staying in another is lodged within it

parts.note: sable is the heraldic name for black
to pend is to hang or be undecided, as in pending

explanation.surface: Cash is there to be spent, as long as your account stays in credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the black' looks like the banking phrase for being in credit, but 'staying in' is the container signal and 'the black' is the heraldic colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Spendable describes funds available for use, as cash is.

clue.text: House well-favoured but unscrupulous guy

parts.note: a villa is a large house
something in favour or in fashion is said to be in

explanation.surface: A handsome mansion owner turns out to be a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wicked person, a rogue without scruples.

clue.text: He demands a price for information, but he's no traitor!

definitions.text: He demands a price for information, but he's no traitor!

parts.words: He demands a price for information, but he's no traitor
parts.note: reads like a double agent selling secrets, but the information is printed papers sold at a shop counter

explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling newspapers is an agent who charges for news, unlike a spy.

clue.text: Tell a couple of pages to get out of bed

parts.note: P is page, and PP two pages
to rise is to get up in the morning

explanation.surface: Inform a pair of servant boys it's time to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pages' looks like young attendants but gives the abbreviation P twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to inform them of something.

clue.text: Have a drink with the players inside when there's mist

indicators.note: inside says one piece is put within another

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: Have a drink with the team in the clubhouse when the windows fog up.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass that steams up becomes clouded with condensation, which is to mist over.

clue.text: No more? Bother!

parts.note: non is Latin and French for no
plus is Latin for more

explanation.surface: Someone exasperated at being told there is none left.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase 'non plus', no more, describes being at a loss: unable to go further.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to perplex or confound them, close to bothering them.

clue.text: Many have just been thorough

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, a crossword sign for many
to own is to have
right means just or fair

explanation.surface: A crowd of people has been completely fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' giving D, the Roman 500, is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright means complete or utter, as does thorough in 'a thorough nuisance'.

clue.text: Didn't at all like the church interior, and so came out

indicators.note: interior says the piece sits inside the other word

parts.note: hated means disliked strongly
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone loathed the inside of the church, so walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Didn't at all like' reads as disapproval of the décor; 'came out' is a chick emerging from its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A chick that has hatched has emerged from the egg.

clue.text: Testing a safety-first saw

indicators.note: first in safety-first picks out the opening letter of safety

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: Trialling a saw that puts safety above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a cutting tool but means a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaying is analysing a metal or ore to test its purity.

clue.text: Outgoing and genuine about conservationists

definitions.note: a noun here, a sum paid out

indicators.note: about says the first word goes round the other

parts.note: real means genuine
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A sociable, sincere person who cares about green campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outgoing' looks like the adjective sociable but is the noun for an expense. NT is the National Trust, which preserves historic houses and land in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental is a payment for hire, one of a household's regular expenses.

clue.text: One of those wanting final sound agreement

definitions.text: One of those wanting final sound agreement

parts.words: One of those wanting final sound agreement
parts.note: sounds like someone seeking a firm deal, but describes a versifier who needs line endings to chime

explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a writer of light verse, whose lines must end on matching sounds.

clue.text: Partisans may well be people with ambition

indicators.note: may well be suggests the letters could become another word once rearranged

explanation.surface: Party supporters are likely to be the ambitious types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may well be' rearranges PARTISANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirants are those who aspire, seeking advancement or a goal.

clue.text: Bag some winnings at Cheltenham

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pocketing a share of one's winnings at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham is a famous English racecourse; 'Bag' looks like a verb, to pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag, traditionally carried by schoolchildren.

clue.text: Danish town where the Spanish go wrong — or take direction

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
to sin is to go morally wrong
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A town where Spaniards either stray or follow instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Spanish' means the Spanish word for 'the'; 'direction' is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore, setting of Hamlet, is the English name for Helsingør, a port in Denmark.

clue.text: After midnight pay attention. Sparkle!

indicators.note: after says the next piece follows the earlier one

parts.note: the middle letter of night is G
to listen is to pay attention

explanation.surface: An order to stay alert after midnight and shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is read as the middle of 'night', its letter G, with LISTEN placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to shine with a glittering light, to sparkle.

clue.text: Found out the left aren't involved

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: It emerged that the political left were not taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges ARENT to EARNT. 'The left' looks political but is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Learnt means discovered or came to know, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Learn as working to produce a magazine

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Studying at work to put out a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges LEARN AS; 'magazine' is not a periodical but a store.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store of weapons and ammunition, which is what a military magazine is.

clue.text: Greenhorns without any bad habits

parts.note: no means without any, as in 'no money'
vices are bad habits

explanation.surface: Beginners have no vices yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' hints at nuns' dress, fitting novices in a convent.
explanation.definitionFit: Novices are beginners or inexperienced people, as greenhorns are.

clue.text: Small coin press that is most excellent

parts.note: a mill presses or grinds
i.e., id est, means that is
ME, Most Excellent, is an honorific abbreviation

explanation.surface: A tiny coin is struck in a press of the highest quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A millieme was a former Egyptian coin worth a thousandth of a pound.

clue.text: A wildly disordered individual can aim to change

indicators.note: to change says the letters swap into a new order

explanation.surface: An unhinged person may be able to reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges CAN AIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniac is a person behaving with wild or frenzied abandon.

clue.text: Allowing a girl to enter a sleazy place

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or club
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: Letting a young woman go into a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first 'a' gives a letter; the second 'a' is a link before 'sleazy place'.
explanation.definitionFit: Admissive means inclined to admit or permit, hence allowing.

clue.text: To keep up suits an eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters go askew

explanation.surface: Indulging an oddball as someone worth keeping up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges SUITS AN.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to maintain or support it.

clue.text: Moulding a cereal, to freeze

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop
to ice is to freeze

explanation.surface: Shaping a breakfast cereal before chilling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moulding' looks like a verb but is the noun, an ornamental strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornice is a decorative moulding running round the top of a wall.

clue.text: A Hellenic heroine will choose military men

parts.note: to elect is to choose
RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment

explanation.surface: A Greek heroine picks soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is a standard crossword source for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra, daughter of Agamemnon, is a central heroine of Greek tragedy.

clue.text: Invariably a number going into a game will appear gloomy

indicators.note: going into says these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: chess is a board game
e'er, poetic for ever, means always
L is the Roman numeral 50

explanation.surface: Losing at every round always makes a player glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going into' puts EERL inside CHESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerless means without joy, dismal or gloomy.
